title: Fifth Motif of the Rose
text:
Where do my words go,

if you no longer hear me?

Where would they go when you heard me?

And when did you hear me?

Never. Lost, lost.

Ah, everything is lost!

You and I lost everything.

We begged for the infinite.

They gave us only the world.

On one side of the waters, on one side of death,

your thirst shone in the dark waters. And today,

what boat comes to your aid? What god embraces you?

With what god do you struggle? I, in the shadows.

I, through the shadows, with the same questions.

For what? For what?

Foolish turnings in fields of vast sands and abundant clouds.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the grief-struck questions, the lost infinity, and the final circling through sand and cloud.

title: Unexpectedly
text:
Unexpectedly the night lights up.

For there is another clarity for what is imagined.

What superhuman face comes on the stems

of absence to open in the night

the dream of its own essence?

What nostalgia remembers itself

and, without wishing to, murmurs its ancient

vestiges of secret happiness?

And what lips open and

—at so tender a distance—

speak of love and death

with words of childhood?

Time dissolves

and nothing is necessary anymore

once you approach, gate of paradise.

Is there night? Is there life? Are there voices?

What terror suddenly consumes us, as we look at each other?

Soul, what is your name?
editorial_note: The translation preserves the sudden illumination and the poem's questions around absence, childhood, paradise, and the soul's name.

title: I Put My Dream on a Ship...
text:
I put my dream on a ship

and the ship upon the sea,

—then I opened the sea with my hands,

to make it shipwreck.


My hands are still wet

with the blue of the half-open waves,

and the color draining from my fingers

colors the deserted sands.


From far away the wind comes,

and the night bends with cold,

under the water my dream is dying

inside a ship...


I will cry all that is necessary

to make the sea grow,

and for my ship to reach the bottom,

and my dream disappear.


Afterward, everything will be perfect;

smooth beach, calm waters,

my eyes dry as stones

and my two hands broken
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker actively wrecking the dream-ship and crying the sea higher until the dream disappears.

title: Life Is Only Possible...
text:
Life is only possible

reinvented.

The sun goes through the fields

and passes its golden hand

over the waters, over the leaves...

Ah, all bubbles

that rise from deep pools

of illusion... — nothing ever.

Ah, all bubbles

But life, life, life,

life is only possible

reinvented.

The moon comes, comes, removes

the chains from my arms.

I project myself through spaces

full of your figure.

Alone, balanced in time,

I detach myself from the swaying

that carries me beyond time.

Alone, in the darkness

I remain: received and given.

Because life, life, life,

life is only possible

reinvented.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Meireles's refrain that life becomes possible only by reinvention, between sun, moon, chains, and darkness.
